parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence and no documented universal-exposure rule for visitors: foreign documents are not shown to be rejected, no bathroom ban, no custody-placement rule, no border screening practice, no evidence of police sweeps against trans travellers. Courts are genuinely protective (2007 Pant ruling, July 2024 recognition order, self-declared third-gender markers), and there is real community infrastructure and visible pride organising. But the operative traveller risk is societal: a November 2024 provincial report documents frequent physical and sexual harassment of visibly trans people in public spaces and government offices, plus rising anti-LGBTQ political hostility — a governing leader's derogatory video and supporters' death threats. No documented working remedy for street violence (no bias-assault prosecutions, no service-complaint recourse), and recourse in practice is court-by-court for residents only. Dated stigma findings (2015) corroborate. Worse than the 0.65 anchors, which show enforced remedies and ordinary service; above the 0.45–0.55 tier, which has universal institutional exclusion or widespread unremedied refusals.
